name: Roasted Lamb Chops with Lemon Potatoes and Peas

components.name: Roasted Lamb Chops

ingredients.name: Raw lamb loin chops bone-in (include bones in purchased weight)

steps: Season lamb chops with olive oil, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Arrange on a separate hot baking sheet without crowding.
Remove the edible lamb meat from bones when calculating actual final cooked yield, and divide lamb, potatoes and peas into six portions.
For meal prep, chill promptly. Keep peas separate from roast lamb to avoid overcooking on reheating.

components.name: Lemon Potatoes

ingredients.name: Raw potatoes cut in 3 cm chunks

steps: Heat oven to 205 C. Toss potato chunks with olive oil, lemon, oregano, salt and stock in a deep tray; cover loosely and roast 25 minutes.

Uncover potatoes and finish roasting another 20-25 minutes until tender with browned edges. Roast lamb chops separately to the desired safe degree of doneness, checking with a thermometer and resting after removing from oven.

components.name: Minted Peas
steps: While the oven finishes, sauté or microwave peas with butter until hot; stir in finely chopped fresh mint and salt.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
Adapted to oven lamb from Food Network’s potato/pea pairing, whose source pan-sears chops. Bone-in purchased weight is not all edible.
Planning: OVEN ADAPTATION: original chops are cooked on stovetop; do not present oven method as source method.
Freezer: roast lamb freezes but may dry on reheating; potatoes soften; peas freeze well
Dietary: Contains dairy; lamb weight includes bones, so macros require meat-only yield measurement.
Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge (≤4°C); refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers, freeze portions for later in the week, and reheat to at least 74°C.
